source_name: SEI-NET (Македонска берза issuer disclosure system) — банки издавачи
why_relevant: Single mandatory disclosure funnel for all listed MK banks (Комерцијална, Стопанска, ТТК, УНИБанка, Силк Роуд, Халкбанк where listed). Price-sensitive announcements and audited annual reports land here first; capex, IT investment and major contract decisions surface as 'други ценовно чувствителни информации' and management addresses. This is the highest-yield pointer for the whole cell.

source_name: Македонска берза — страница на издавач: Комерцијална банка АД Скопје
why_relevant: Per-issuer index of audited/unaudited financial statements and price-sensitive filings, with an RSS feed. Notes to the accounts carry intangible-assets and equipment capex movement — the only quantitative read on a private bank's IT/hardware spend.

source_name: Комерцијална банка АД Скопје — Финансиски извештаи / Односи со инвеститори
why_relevant: Largest MK bank (now in NLB group orbit) with no tender page at all; its annual reports and IR section are the only disclosure of investment in equipment/software and of large project decisions.

source_name: Стопанска банка АД Скопје — Податоци и извештаи
why_relevant: NBG/OTP-owned systemic bank; no procurement page exists on the site (verified by navigation inventory), so reports + news are the only disclosure surface for vendor and capex signals.

source_name: NLB Banka АД Скопје — корпоративен сајт
why_relevant: Post-merger with Komercijalna, the biggest buying centre in the market. No local tender page was found; sourcing is expected to be run at NLB Group level, so this site mainly yields news of go-lives and vendor partnerships that reveal awards after the fact.

source_name: NLB Group — Јавни разписи (investor/public tenders section)
why_relevant: Group-level publication channel of the parent of NLB Banka Skopje (and now Komercijalna). Group-wide sourcing decisions for core banking, cards and IT are taken in Ljubljana; anything published here can determine what the MK subsidiary buys.

source_name: Halkbank АД Скопје — корпоративен сајт
why_relevant: Turkish-owned systemic bank. No procurement/tender section surfaced in mk-language search; monitoring is limited to news, branch-network expansion (a capex proxy) and annual reports. Parent Türkiye Halk Bankası runs its own supplier processes.

source_name: Sparkasse Bank Makedonija — About us / Sale of property
why_relevant: The only 'call for offers' style publication found on this bank's site is foreclosed-asset sales, not procurement — a useful negative benchmark and a demonstration that MK banks use оглас/повик only for selling, not buying. Still worth tracking because the same page template is where a procurement call would appear if ever published.

source_name: ProCredit Bank АД Скопје — корпоративен сајт
why_relevant: Sister ProCredit banks (Georgia, Ukraine) publish open tender pages for IT services under a documented group 'value for money' tender policy, so the MK entity plausibly runs comparable tenders even though no MK tender page was located. Worth periodic manual re-checking and direct outreach.

source_name: ProCredit group sister-bank tender pages (Georgia/Ukraine) as template
why_relevant: Concrete evidence of what a ProCredit bank tenders for (loan origination systems, penetration testing) and how it words its calls. Gives the vocabulary and the shape of any MK-entity call, and reveals the group's shortlisted vendor universe.

source_name: УНИБанка АД Скопје — Годишни извештаи (Редовно собрание)
why_relevant: UNIBank publishes full annual reports as PDFs on its own domain, and these explicitly narrate capex items (e.g. vehicle fleet purchase, photovoltaic plant installation) — proof that annual reports do carry procurement-level detail for the mid-tier MK banks.

source_name: ТТК Банка АД Скопје — За банката / Организација
why_relevant: Small listed bank; site carries organisational structure (identifies the IT and logistics owners who would run sourcing) but no tender section. Combine with its MSE issuer feed for report-level capex.

source_name: biznisinfo.mk — банкарски проектни и вендор вести
why_relevant: Covers bank product/technology go-lives (e.g. citizen-bond distribution through Komercijalna) which retro-reveal which vendor/system was procured. Award-notice substitute in a market with no award notices.

source_name: НБРСМ — регистар/вести за банки (профили на банките)
why_relevant: Canonical legal names, ownership and licence status for every bank in the cell — the actor map backbone needed to normalise aliases (Халкбанка / Halk Banka / Halkbank AD Skopje; НЛБ Тутунска / NLB Banka; Универзална Инвестициона Банка / УНИБанка).

source_name: Printec Group — North Macedonia country page & news
why_relevant: Printec (present in MK since 2006) is a principal ATM/self-service, cash-management and unattended-payments integrator for MK banks and retailers; its country page and case studies name customers (e.g. Komercijalna Banka, Vita Bite unattended POS) and therefore reveal installed base, renewals and de-facto contract awards that buyers never publish.

source_name: Asseco SEE / ASEE — corporate news and MK subsidiary
why_relevant: ASEE (formerly Pexim, Skopje) is one of the largest banking-software suppliers in SEE with a substantial MK development and delivery centre; its news/press section and investor reporting announce banking-software and payment contracts, which is the most direct vendor-side evidence of MK bank IT awards.

source_name: Payten — news & events (ASEE payments brand)
why_relevant: Payten publishes granular 'delivered/implemented/signed' announcements naming banks and terminal volumes across SEE (e.g. Credins Bank Albania POS delivery, Bank Poštanska Štedionica Android POS). The same feed is the highest-yield channel for any MK POS/acquiring/ATM-managed-services award. No MK-specific item was found in this pass — a monitoring, not a one-shot, source.

source_name: CaSys International (International Card System AD Skopje) — services & about
why_relevant: Domestic card processor serving roughly eleven MK banks (NLB, Poštenska, Sparkasse, Export & Credit and others) and certified by Mastercard/Visa; its own site enumerates client banks and new mandates (e.g. becoming Diners Club processor in MK). A vendor-side register of who processes for whom, i.e. of long-running outsourcing contracts.

source_name: Nextsense (Skopje) — digital banking / eID references
why_relevant: MK-headquartered vendor of eID and digital-banking onboarding; its OneID service with KIBS is deployed at Komercijalna Banka for remote client identification and account opening. Vendor announcements are the only public trace of these bank IT engagements.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom — Europe (North Macedonia items)
why_relevant: Scheme-side press releases name MK counterparties and go-lives (national Digital Identity Service with MISA, ID Service operated by Evrotrust with NLB Bank Skopje as first adopter and UNIBank Skopje following). Scheme announcements often precede or accompany bank-side procurement.

source_name: Evrotrust — blog / partnership announcements (MK ID Service operator)
why_relevant: Operator of the Mastercard-branded ID Service in MK; publishes milestone posts naming MK bank clients (NLB Bank Skopje, UNIBank Skopje) — vendor-side evidence of onboarding/eKYC contracts with MK banks.

source_name: MASIT — Macedonian ICT Chamber member directory
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map for MK IT suppliers. Member profiles (ASEE Group, CaSys International, and others) give the candidate vendor universe from which customer-reference and press pages can be harvested — the seed list for the whole cell.

source_name: AmCham North Macedonia — member directory
why_relevant: Second independent vendor register that captures international suppliers operating locally (Asseco SEE, International Card Systems/CaSys listed). Useful to cross-fill gaps in MASIT and to obtain local legal entity names used in contract records.
